justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A warning-first base R6 design could have retained the R4 regex temporarily while declaring non-space whitespace non-canonical, but it would not fully enforce the single-space datatype rule.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve rare legacy values with tabs or newlines, at the cost of prolonging a mismatch between prose conformance and computable validation for a widely used primitive.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: both R4 and R6 define `code` as having no whitespace other than single spaces, while the R4 regex could accept other whitespace through `\s`. Changing the regex separator to a literal space is therefore a computable correction to match the datatype definition, not an arbitrary semantic narrowing. Because the affected legacy values were already inconsistent with the prose rule and are likely rare, the level of breakage is probably justified even though a softer transition was technically possible.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base-design alternative would be to keep `[^\s]+(\s[^\s]+)*` for one R6 cycle and add warning-level conformance text or a best-practice invariant saying that internal whitespace must be ordinary single spaces. That would preserve most R4-valid instances, including values with tabs or newlines between tokens, while giving implementers time to clean data. It is only a partial alternative because it does not meet the enforcement goal: base R6 validators would still accept values the datatype prose says should not exist, and this inconsistency would apply everywhere the primitive `code` is used.
